title: ST. ELMO MAN FACES CHARGES
full_story:
A St. Elmo man is facing four new Felony counts in Fayette County Court, following his arrest over the weekend.

51-year-old Curtis D. Jennings is facing two drug charges, one is Unlawful Possession with Intent to Deliver 5 to 15 grams of Methamphetamine, a Class 1 Felony.  He also faces a charge of Unlawful Possession of Methamphetamine of 5 to 15 grams, which is a Class 2 Felony.

Jennings is also facing a charge of Theft of between $10,000 and $100,000, which is a Class 2 Felony.  Information on the charge says Jennings is alleged to have stolen copper wire from Petco Petroleum in excess of $10,000.  Jennings also faces a Class 3 Felony for Unlawful Possession of a Weapon by a Felon.  Information on the charge states that Jennings is alleged to have possessed ammunition and Jennings had previously been convicted of a Felony in Effingham County in 2019.

In Fayette County Court Monday, the court found that the state had met their burden that Jennings had committed a detainable offense.  The court found that due to Jennings’ behavior and the charges against him that he did pose a threat to the public.  The court also stated that Jennings is currently on pre-trial release for two other Felonies and that no condition or combination of conditions will mitigate the threat posed by Jennings.

Jennings remains in the Fayette County Jail.  He will make a pre-trial appearance on April 7th at 9 am.

title: KRISTA PHILLIPS INTRODUCED
full_story:
The Miss Illinois County Fair Queen was honored in the Illinois House of Representatives on Tuesday as a part of Agriculture Legislative Day at the State Capitol.

Representative Brad Halbrook of Shelbyville introduced Krista Phillips, 21, of Effingham.  Phillips was chosen from 75 contestants in January to be the Miss Illinois County Fair.  Phillips also met with FFA members and toured the capitol.

Phillips will graduate from the University of Illinois-Champaign in May with a bachelor’s degree in business management and marketing.  She plans to return to Effingham and pursue her dream of opening a small business.

title: OCC MUSICAL
full_story:
Olney Central College Theater’s production of the musical Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat opens on Friday at the Dr. John D. Stull Performing Arts Center.

The production marks the return of the beloved musical to the OCC stage for the first time in 18 years.  Known for its lively music and colorful storytelling, Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat retells the familiar biblical story of Joseph, his famous coat of many colors, and his journey from hardship to triumph.

This year’s production brings together a large community cast spanning generations.  Performers range in age from 15 to their mid-70s, and the show features a 50-member children’s choir, adding extra energy and excitement to the show.

While audiences will recognize the classic story and many of the well-known songs, this OCC Theater production also has a few surprises along the way.

The production is fun and accessible for audiences of all ages, making it a family-friendly night at the theater.

Performances will take place on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday, at 7 pm and on Sunday, at 2 pm, at the Dr. John D. Stull Performing Arts Center on the Olney Central College campus.

Tickets are $14 for reserved seating and are available now at www.iecc.edu/occ/theater or by calling 618-395-7777, ext. 2408.

title: SUMMER JOBS PROGRAM
full_story:
The Illinois Secretary of State’s Office is now accepting applications for its fourth annual summer job program.

Approximately 120 paid positions are available for college, trade school, and graduate students, as well as graduating high school seniors who will be enrolled in college or trade school in the fall.  A limited program is also available for 25 high school students ages 16 and older with all the positions offered across the Secretary of State’s 25 departments and at DMV facilities throughout the state.

Applications are now being accepted at the Secretary of State’s website, at ilsos.gov.summerjobs where applicants must submit a resume, completed application, and a cover letter describing their interest in working at the Secretary of State’s Office, plus applicants can list up to three preferred work locations.

title: ENERGY ASSISTANCE AVAILABLE
full_story:
The Energy Assistance Foundation, through its Warm Neighbors Cool Friends (WNCF) program, partners with CEFS Economic Opportunity to provide energy bill payment assistance to eligible Ameren Illinois customers in Clay, Christian, Effingham, Fayette, Montgomery, Moultrie and Shelby counties.  In December 2025, Ameren Illinois contributed an additional $2 million to support Illinois households in 2026, ensuring more families can keep the lights on, stay warm in the winter, and cool in the summer.

Through this program, eligible households may receive up to $500 in assistance during the heating season, and up to $400 during the cooling season.

A matching customer payment made within the last 45 days is required.  The WNCF program serves income-qualified households who may not qualify for federal assistance but are still facing real financial strain.  Eligibility includes customers with household incomes between 200% and 300% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) or up to 80% of the county’s Area Median Income (AMI).

“This program is about peace of mind,” said Susan Sams, Executive Director of the Energy Assistance Foundation.  “Warm Neighbors Cool Friends is a critical lifeline for hardworking families who are doing their best but still need help covering essential energy costs.”

Funding is limited and applications are required.  Residents are encouraged to apply as soon as possible to ensure they don’t miss out on available assistance.

For more information and to apply visit www.warmneighborscoolfriends.org/  OR http://www.cefseoc.org/liheap

title: THE CHICKS AT STATE FAIR
full_story:
The Illinois State Fair announced that the Superstar Trio The Chicks will take the Illinois Lottery Grandstand Stage on Saturday, August 22nd, bringing their powerhouse vocals and award-winning catalog to an already stacked Grandstand line-up.

Earning universal recognition as the biggest-selling US female band of all time, The Chicks have sold more than 30.5 million albums and are among an elite group of artists, and the only female group, to achieve multiple “diamond” selling, ten million copies, releases.  The trio, Natalie Maines, Martie Maguire, and Emily Strayer, has received 13 GRAMMY Awards, six Billboard Music Awards, four American Music Awards, and numerous Country Music Association Awards, among many other accolades throughout their groundbreaking career.  Since their breakout album Wide Open Spaces, the band has delivered hit after hit, including fan favorites like “Cowboy Take Me Away,” “Landslide,” and “Not Ready to Make Nice.”  Known for their tight harmonies, masterful musicianship, and powerful live performances, The Chicks continue to connect with audiences across generations.

“We’re proud to continue bringing top tier entertainment to the Illinois State Fair, and The Chicks are a fantastic addition to this year’s lineup,” said Illinois Department of Agriculture Director Jerry Costello II.  “Their music has stood the test of time and continues to resonate with fans of all ages.  We’re excited to welcome them to Springfield this August.”

After a nearly 14-year hiatus, The Chicks released their fifth studio album Gaslighter in July 2020 via Columbia Records.  The 12-track record was co-produced by award-winning singer-songwriter and producer Jack Antonoff and has been hailed as some of the band’s most uninhibited, modern, progressive, and original work to date, reaffirming their place as one of the most influential groups in music.

“The Chicks are known for putting on an unforgettable show,” said Illinois State Fair Manager Rebecca Clark.  “With a catalog of songs that so many people know and love, this will be a special night at the Grandstand that fairgoers won’t want to miss.”

Tickets for The Chicks will go on sale Saturday, at 10 am via Ticketmaster.  Tier 3 tickets are $88, Tier 2 tickets are $93, Tier 1 tickets are $113, Track tickets are $128, and Blue Ribbon tickets are $168.  A $30 Pre-Show Party ticket is offered as an additional upgrade for all paid concerts.

Mark your calendars for the 2026 Illinois State Fair, August 13th through 23rd in Springfield.

title: INSURANCE BILL
full_story:
A bill giving the Illinois Department of Insurance authority to review and regulate premiums for both auto and homeowners insurance passed the House last week and now awaits Senate action.

Two proposals, which started as separate pieces of legislation, were combined into a single bill that passed the House March 19th.  The combined bill now awaits Senate approval before being sent to Governor JB Pritzker.

Pritzker initially called for rate review authority over homeowners insurance last summer after Bloomington-based State Farm Insurance announced it was raising rates in Illinois an average 27.2%, citing losses it had incurred from weather-related disasters in the state.

Pritzker, however, questioned that rationale.  He and legislative leaders suggested the company may have been shifting losses from disasters in other states onto Illinois consumers.  He also used the controversy to highlight the fact that, unlike most other states, Illinois exercises no control over insurance premiums and has no law prohibiting excessive, inadequate or unfairly discriminatory rates in the insurance industry.

Separately, Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias has been pushing for reforms in the automobile insurance sector, arguing insurance companies were setting rates based on factors such as a person’s credit rating that have little or nothing to do with their driving record.

Neither bill made it through the General Assembly in 2025.  A bill regulating homeowners insurance passed the Senate during the fall veto session in October but failed on the floor of the House just before lawmakers adjourned.

The bill that emerged in the House last week was the product of continued negotiations among lawmakers and the governor’s office, although the insurance industry says it still opposes the final product.

Senate Bill 1486, as amended by the House, would prohibit companies from charging “excessive, inadequate or unfairly discriminatory” rates for auto and homeowners insurance.  And, starting July 1st, 2027, it would require them to give consumers at least 60 days’ notice before raising premiums 10% or more.

It would also establish a procedure for the Insurance Department to review and approve new rate filings after July 1st, 2027.  Although companies would still be allowed to file new rates and begin collecting premiums under those terms immediately, the department would have authority to review those rates.

The Illinois Insurance Association, the American Property Casualty Insurance Association and the National Association of Mutual Insurance Companies issued a joint statement following the House vote saying the bill represented “one of the most sweeping and harmful insurance regulatory overhauls in state history” and that it would end up harming Illinois consumers.
